docs.title: NHIS Data Documentation
docs.text: Welcome! This site is an unofficial guide to the research databases of the Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS, 국민건강보험공단).

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
The NHIS releases these databases through its data sharing service, but the documentation that comes with them is patchy, not version-controlled, and often limited to short variable lists. Many variables are self-explanatory, while others mean something different from what their names suggest, and researchers usually learn these differences by trial and error.

The goal of this website is to collect all the public information and knowledge on the NHIS databases, combined with hands-on experience working with the data, in one place, including variable definitions, guidance on constructing analysis samples, and known caveats.

It is modeled on the documentation that the Research Data Assistance Center (ResDAC) provides for Medicare data and on Kyle Barron's Medicare documentation.

docs.title: What is on this site
docs.text:
The site has five parts.

  • Program and data describes the health insurance system that generates the data, the family of NHIS research databases, and the application process.
  • Datasets has one page per database, covering sample design, versions, and linkage.
  • Variables documents each table and variable, with Korean and English labels, value codes, and notes.
  • Working with the data is a series of short posts on practical issues, such as merging the tables, building an analysis sample, and the caveats that commonly lead to mistakes.
  • Glossary translates the Korean administrative terms used in the data and the official documentation.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text: This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the NHIS. Entries are written by researchers who use the data and may contain errors, so check them against the documentation that comes with your extract before relying on them.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Corrections, additions, and blog posts are welcome from anyone who has worked with the data, and the easiest way to send them is an email to sihopark@kdischool.ac.kr. The contributing page explains what to include and how the codebook files are organized.

Maintained by Siho Park, KDI School of Public Policy and Management.

docs.text: The official documentation and variable labels are written in Korean administrative language. This page gives the English translations used on this site, so that the same Korean term is always translated the same way.

docs.title: How to cite
docs.text:
If this site helped your research, please cite it as follows.

Park, Siho. NHIS Data Documentation. https://siho-park.github.io/nhis-documentation/. Accessed [date].

Please also cite the cohort profile or data resource profile of the database you use, listed on the references page, since those papers describe the official sample design.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions from researchers who have used the data are what make this site useful. A correction to a single value code saves the next user the same afternoon of detective work.

docs.title: Suggesting a correction
docs.text: The simplest way to suggest a change is an email to sihopark@kdischool.ac.kr. Please include the link to the page, the change you propose, and its source if there is one, such as a manual, a published paper, or your own experience with the data.

docs.title: Writing a post
docs.text: Researchers who have worked with the data are welcome to write a post for Working with the data. A post can be short and cover a single pitfall, a way of constructing a variable, or a lesson from the application or export process. Send the draft by email to sihopark@kdischool.ac.kr in any format, such as Word, Google Docs, or plain text, together with your name and affiliation as they should appear on the post. The draft is then formatted for the site and published under your name.

docs.title: Using GitHub
docs.text:
Contributors who use GitHub can also suggest a change there directly.

  • Open an issue. Describe the problem or the missing information in a GitHub issue.
  • Edit the page. Every page has an edit button at the top right that opens its source file on GitHub, where you can propose the change as a pull request. On a variable page, the button opens the file for the whole table, and the fields of each entry are described below.

docs.title: What not to post
docs.text: Never post individual-level records, screenshots of the analysis environment, or statistics computed from the data that have not passed the NHIS export review (반출 심사). Describing the structure of a variable, its codes, and its pitfalls is fine, but numbers from the data should be limited to results that have already been cleared for release, such as published tables.

docs.title: How the variable pages are built
docs.text:
The variable pages are generated from YAML files in the codebook/ folder of the repository, with one folder per dataset and one file per table. Editing a variable means editing its entry in the YAML file, and the pages are rebuilt automatically.

codebook/
  nsc/
    _dataset.yml    dataset title, years, and source documents
    _codes.yml      shared code lists, such as district codes
    bnc.yml         eligibility and premium table
    t20.yml         claim statement table
    ...

The YAML files are produced by the importer in tools/importer/, which reads the NHIS layout files and manuals, applies the corrections in curate.py, and adds the English translations kept in tools/translations.tsv. The importer can be run again when the NHIS publishes new documentation, and it leaves alone any variable whose status is verified or that carries keep: true.

docs.text:
Field Required Meaning name yes Variable name as it appears in the data label_ko, label_en yes Korean label from the official documentation and an English translation status yes documented, verified, unverified, or disputed, used by the importer and not shown on the site verified_by, verified_on if verified Name of the person who checked the entry and the date, as YYYY-MM-DD type, years no Storage type and the years in which the variable exists notes no List of notes in English, shown in a box at the top of the page periods no One entry per span of years in which the documentation describes the variable the same way related no Links to other variables, written VAR, table.VAR, or dataset.table.VAR keep no true to protect a hand-edited entry from the importer

Each period has years, label_ko, and label_en, and optionally a description and notes (lists of items with en and ko), codes (a list with code, label_ko, and label_en), and code_list (the name of a list in _codes.yml).

docs.title: Previewing the site locally
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs and the Material theme. Install the requirements and start the local server, which rebuilds the site whenever a file changes.

pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

The site is then available at http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: Working with the data
docs.text:
These posts cover the practical side of the NHIS data, from merging the tables to the caveats that the official variable lists do not mention. They are written for researchers who are new to the data, and each post can be read on its own. The examples use the variable names of the National Sample Cohort 2.2, and the variable name crosswalk lists the names used in the other databases.

Researchers who have worked with the data are welcome to share what they have learned, and a post can be as short as a single pitfall. Send a draft in any format to sihopark@kdischool.ac.kr, as described on the contributing page.

docs.title: How the NHIS tables fit together
docs.text: An NHIS extract arrives as a set of separate tables, and almost every project begins by merging them. Each table describes a different kind of record, such as a person in a year, a claim, or a diagnosis on a claim, and a few identifiers tie the records together. This post explains what one row of each table stands for and which variables to merge on.

docs.title: What one row stands for
docs.text:
Knowing what one row of a table represents, its unit of observation, is the first step before any merge. The table below lists the unit of each main table in the National Sample Cohort (표본코호트DB).

Table 한글 One row per BNC, eligibility and premiums 자격 및 보험료 Person and year BND, birth and death 출생 및 사망 Person T20, claim statements 명세서 Claim T30, treatment details 진료내역 Line item on a claim, such as a procedure, a test, or a drug administered at the provider T40, diagnoses 상병내역 Diagnosis on a claim T60, prescriptions 처방전교부상세내역 Drug on a prescription issued for a pharmacy G1E, general health screening 건강검진 Screening INST, healthcare providers 요양기관 Provider and year

The claim statement table T20 is the hub of the claims data. It records the person, the provider, the start date of care, the primary and secondary diagnoses, the days of care, and the amounts, while the other claims tables add detail to each claim.

docs.title: The identifiers that link the tables
docs.text:
Three identifiers and a year variable do almost all of the linking between these tables. The cohort databases use other names for the same keys, which are listed in the variable name crosswalk.

Variable 한글 English Found in RN_INDI 개인고유번호 Person identifier Every table except INST and the long-term care facility table T05 RN_KEY 청구고유번호 Claim identifier T20, T30, T40, and T60 RN_INST 요양기관고유번호 Provider identifier T20 and INST STD_YYYY 기준연도 Reference year BNC, T20, and INST

The diagram shows how the tables connect. Each line joins two tables and is labeled with the merge key, and the fork at one end marks the table with many rows for each value of the key.

erDiagram
    BND ||--o{ BNC : "RN_INDI"
    BNC ||--o{ T20 : "RN_INDI, STD_YYYY"
    BNC ||--o{ G1E : "RN_INDI, year"
    INST ||--o{ T20 : "RN_INST, STD_YYYY"
    T20 ||--o{ T30 : "RN_KEY"
    T20 ||--o{ T40 : "RN_KEY"
    T20 ||--o{ T60 : "RN_KEY"

docs.title: Five merges that cover most analyses
docs.text:
Most analyses need only a handful of merges, and each one has a fixed key.

  • Claims and their details. T30, T40, and T60 link to T20 on RN_KEY. Each claim has many rows in a detail table, so the merged data have one row per line item, diagnosis, or drug.
  • Claims and people. T20 links to BNC on RN_INDI and STD_YYYY. The eligibility table has one row per person per year, which is why T20 carries its own reference year for this merge.
  • Birth and death. BND links to BNC on RN_INDI alone, since BND has one row per person with the year of birth BTH_YYYY (출생년도) and the year and month of death DTH_YYYYMM (사망연월).
  • Health screening. G1E links to BNC on RN_INDI, with the year of screening EXMD_BZ_YYYY (검진년도) matched to STD_YYYY. Most people are invited for screening every two years, so a person-year panel has screening values only in screening years and leaves the other years empty.
  • Providers. INST links to T20 on RN_INST and STD_YYYY. Provider characteristics such as the type of institution, the number of beds, and staffing change over time, so the year of the claim matters.

docs.title: The merge to avoid
docs.text:
The one merge that almost never makes sense joins two detail tables to each other. T30 and T40 both have many rows per claim, so merging them on RN_KEY pairs every line item with every diagnosis on the same claim. A claim with three diagnoses and ten line items becomes thirty rows, and any sum over line items is tripled.

The safe pattern is to collapse each detail table to one row per claim first, for example to an indicator for a diagnosis or a total per claim, and then merge the result onto T20. Counting the rows before and after each merge is a quick check, since a merge that adds information about claims should not change the number of claims. In Stata, merge 1:1 and merge m:1 stop with an error when the key is not unique where it should be, which catches this mistake early.

docs.title: Shortcuts through the detail tables
docs.text: The detail tables also carry the person identifier, so some person-level measures can skip T20. T30, T40, and T60 each include RN_INDI, and T30 and T40 also include the start date of care MDCARE_STRT_DT (요양개시일자). The reference year STD_YYYY and the provider identifier RN_INST appear only in T20, however, so any measure by reference year or by provider still goes through the claim statement table.

docs.title: The long-term care tables
docs.text:
The long-term care tables form a separate group, linked by identifiers of their own.

  • The long-term care application identifier RN_INDI_SEQ (장기요양신청 일련번호) links the applications and results table T01 (장기요양 신청 및 판정결과), the assessment items table T02 (장기요양 인정조사사항), and the long-term care claims table T04 (장기요양 청구명세서). It is RN_INDI followed by a three-digit application number, and the three tables also carry RN_INDI for linking to the rest of the database.
  • The long-term care facility number LTC_INST_ID (장기요양시설번호) links T04 to the facility table T05 (장기요양기관 현황). T05 also carries the reference year and month STD_YYYYMM (기준년월), so check how many rows each facility has before merging.

docs.title: Files to append first
docs.text: In the National Sample Cohort, each claims table comes as several files that need to be appended before any merge. The files are split by type of care, namely medical care (M), dental care (D), Korean medicine (K), and pharmacies (P), and each type is split again into periods, such as NSC2_M20_0215, NSC2_M20_1619, and NSC2_M20_2023. The files of one table share the same layout, and the full file list is on the dataset page of the codebook.

docs.title: Building an analysis sample
docs.text: Most projects with NHIS data follow people over time, so the first real task is a panel with one row per person and year. The key decision is where that panel comes from. It should be built from the eligibility table, not from the claims tables, because people who use no care in a year have no claims and would otherwise vanish from the sample.

docs.title: Why the claims are the wrong place to start
docs.text:
A panel built from the claims contains only people who used care, which distorts almost any average computed from it. A person with no visits in a year has no claims in that year, so the person-year is missing rather than recorded as zero. Average spending per person computed from such a panel describes people who saw a provider and overstates spending in the population.

The eligibility and premium table BNC (자격 및 보험료) avoids this problem, because it has one row per person per year whether or not the person used care. Starting from BNC keeps the people who used no care in the sample, with zeros for their outcomes.

docs.title: Three steps to a person-year panel
docs.text:
The construction has three steps, and each step works on a different part of the data. The post on how the tables fit together explains the merge keys used along the way.

First, define the population and the observation window in the eligibility table BNC. Restrictions on age, sex, region, insurance type, and years are applied here, and the year and month of death DTH_YYYYMM (사망연월) in the birth and death table BND (출생 및 사망) determine the last year in which a person is at risk.

Second, compute outcomes in the claims tables at the claim level, such as an indicator for a diagnosis or the amount paid. Then collapse them to the person and year, using the person identifier RN_INDI (개인고유번호) and either the reference year STD_YYYY (기준연도) or the year of the start date of care MDCARE_STRT_DT (요양개시일자).

Finally, merge the person-year outcomes onto the eligibility panel and fill the person-years without a match with zeros. A missing person-year at this stage means that the person used no covered care, not that the data are missing, and the post on non-covered services explains why the word covered matters.

docs.title: Choices that shape the sample
docs.text:
Two further choices change who is in the sample and how their outcomes compare, and both are worth stating in the paper.

  • Left censoring. The data begin in 2002, so a condition first observed in 2002 may have begun earlier. Studies of new cases usually exclude people with the condition in a washout period at the start of the data.
  • Deaths. Outcomes in the year of death cover only part of the year, so annual outcomes in that year are not comparable with those of survivors unless they are scaled by time at risk.

docs.title: Non-covered services are missing from the claims
docs.text: The NHIS claims record only the care that insurance pays for, and this limit shapes every measure of spending and utilization. Services that patients pay for entirely out of pocket are never billed to the insurer, so they leave no trace in the data.

docs.title: Covered and non-covered services
docs.text: Korean health insurance divides medical services into two groups, and only one of them produces claims. Covered services (급여) are billed to the insurer, and the patient pays a share of the cost. Non-covered services (비급여) are paid for entirely by the patient, so they are not billed to the insurer and do not appear in the claims.

docs.title: What the claims can and cannot measure
docs.text:
Spending measured from the claims is covered spending, which falls short of what patients actually spend on care. The claim statement table T20 (명세서) records the total covered cost after review ED_RC_TOT_AMT (심결요양급여비용총액), divided into patient cost sharing EDC_SBA (심결본인부담금) and the insurer payment EDC_INSUR_BRDN_AMT (심결보험자부담금). None of these amounts include spending on non-covered services.

Utilization measured from the claims is understated for the same reason. A service paid for entirely out of pocket generates no claim, so it is missing from counts of services as well as from spending.

The patient cost sharing variable needs particular care in the write-up. EDC_SBA records what patients paid toward covered services only, while total out-of-pocket spending also includes everything paid for non-covered services. EDC_SBA is therefore a lower bound on out-of-pocket spending rather than a measure of it.

docs.title: Why the gap matters for comparisons
docs.text: The gap varies across conditions, provider types, and years, which matters more than its average size. A comparison across any of these dimensions mixes differences in care with differences in the share of care that is non-covered. A trend in covered spending, for example, can reflect services moving into or out of coverage rather than a change in the care people receive.

docs.title: What to do in practice
docs.text:
Three habits keep the gap from distorting the results.

  • Name the measure precisely. Describe outcomes as covered spending or covered utilization, in the text and in the titles of tables and figures.
  • Report cost sharing for what it is. Describe EDC_SBA as patient cost sharing for covered services, not as total out-of-pocket spending.
  • Check comparisons for differences in coverage. When comparing conditions, provider types, or years, consider whether the non-covered share is likely to differ between the groups, since the claims cannot measure that difference.

docs.title: Identifying conditions from diagnosis codes
docs.text: A diagnosis code on a claim looks like a diagnosis, but it is recorded to justify payment rather than to confirm a condition. A code can appear because a condition was confirmed, because it was suspected and a test was ordered to rule it out, or because it qualifies the claim for a particular payment rule. A single claim with a code is therefore weak evidence that a person has the condition.

docs.title: Common definitions
docs.text:
Studies with NHIS data therefore define a condition by a combination of claims rather than by a single code. The definitions below are common in the literature, listed from least to most restrictive.

  • Any claim. At least one claim with the code in any diagnosis position. This maximizes sensitivity but counts rule-out diagnoses.
  • Repeated or inpatient claims. At least two outpatient claims, or one inpatient claim, with the code. This is the most common definition for chronic conditions.
  • Diagnosis plus treatment. A claim with the code together with a prescription or procedure specific to the condition, such as an antidiabetic drug for diabetes.

The choice should follow a published validation study whenever one exists for the condition.

docs.title: Where the diagnoses are stored
docs.text: A definition based only on the claim statement table misses diagnoses recorded in later positions on the claim. The claim statement table T20 (명세서) stores the primary diagnosis SICK_SYM1 (주상병) and one secondary diagnosis SICK_SYM2 (부상병), while the diagnosis table T40 (상병내역) stores every diagnosis on the claim in MCEX_SICK_SYM (요양급여상병기호). The difference matters most for chronic conditions, which are rarely the reason for a visit.

docs.title: Masked diagnoses
docs.text: Some conditions cannot be identified in the National Sample Cohort at all, because their codes are masked. In the cohort, 3,116 sensitive diagnosis codes, including mental disorders, pregnancy and childbirth, and notifiable infectious diseases, show only their first letter followed by an underscore. The NHIS directs studies of these conditions to the customized research DB, as described on the dataset page.

docs.title: Special co-payment registration
docs.text: For cancer and several other serious conditions, registration for a reduced co-payment offers a more specific marker than diagnosis codes. Patients with these conditions can register for a reduced co-payment (산정특례), and registration requires medical confirmation.

docs.title: Code revisions
docs.text: Diagnosis codes follow the Korean Classification of Diseases (KCD), a Korean adaptation of ICD-10 that has been revised several times. A code list written for one revision should be checked against the revision in force in each year of the data.

docs.title: Counting visits, admissions, and spending
docs.text: A claim is a billing unit, so a count of claims is not a count of visits or admissions. Measures of utilization and spending need to account for how care is split into claims, and the splitting differs by setting and has changed over time.

docs.title: Outpatient visits
docs.text:
Counts of outpatient claims can change even when the number of visits does not. In the National Sample Cohort, outpatient billing moved from one claim per month to one claim per visit day, a change extended to hospitals in 2011, as noted on the dataset page. The claim statement table T20 (명세서) also records the days of visits or inpatient days on each claim in VSHSP_DD_CNT (입내원일수).

Drugs dispensed at a pharmacy are billed on separate pharmacy claims, apart from the visit that generated the prescription. Counting pharmacy claims as visits therefore counts the same visit twice.

docs.title: Inpatient admissions
docs.text: A long inpatient stay can be billed on several claims, so counting inpatient claims overstates admissions. Admissions are usually reconstructed by linking inpatient claims for the same person and provider whose dates of care are contiguous or overlap.

docs.title: Spending
docs.text:
The amount fields of the claim statement table measure covered spending after review, which differs from the amount the provider originally claimed. The total covered cost after review ED_RC_TOT_AMT (심결요양급여비용총액) is divided into patient cost sharing EDC_SBA (심결본인부담금) and the insurer payment EDC_INSUR_BRDN_AMT (심결보험자부담금).

  • Reviewed and claimed amounts. Use the amounts after review rather than the amounts originally claimed by the provider, since only the reviewed amounts were paid.
  • Pharmacy spending. Drugs dispensed at a pharmacy are billed on separate pharmacy claims, so dropping pharmacy claims omits most outpatient drug spending.
  • Inflation. Amounts are in nominal won and should be deflated before comparing years.
  • Non-covered services. Spending on non-covered services (비급여) is not in the data at all, as the post on non-covered services explains.

docs.title: Five pitfalls to check before you start
docs.text: Some features of the NHIS data are easy to miss, because nothing in the variable names reveals them. The larger caveats have their own posts, on non-covered services, diagnosis codes, counting visits and admissions, and people without claims. This post collects five smaller ones that are worth checking before the analysis begins.

docs.title: The premium decile is not an income decile
docs.text: Premiums are computed from wages for employee insured and from income and property for self-employed insured, and dependents take the decile of the person they depend on. The same decile therefore corresponds to different incomes across insurance types. The National Sample Cohort page describes further features of CTRB_Q10 (보험료분위 10분위, premium decile), including the shifts after the 2018 and 2022 premium reforms.

docs.title: Variable names change across releases
docs.text: Different releases of the same database use different names for many variables, so code written for one release does not run on another without changes. Check the release before reusing code from a paper or a colleague.

docs.title: Identifiers do not link across databases
docs.text: Each release has its own pseudonymized person identifier, so the same person cannot be followed from one database to another. The data also cannot be linked to external sources without a separate approval. See RN_INDI (개인고유번호, person identifier) in the National Sample Cohort.

docs.title: Diagnosis and district codes change over time
docs.text: Diagnosis codes follow successive revisions of the Korean Classification of Diseases, and district codes change when administrative boundaries are redrawn. Both need a crosswalk before comparisons across years. The district code list of the National Sample Cohort, for example, lists the districts of Gangwon under province code 42 and again under 51, the code of 강원특별자치도 (Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province) from 2023.

docs.title: Results must pass export review
docs.text: Nothing leaves the analysis environment without passing the NHIS export review (반출 심사), which applies rules on minimum cell sizes. Plan the tables and figures in advance, since each export request takes time. See Applying for data.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
The NHIS offers several research databases that differ in population, sampling, and variable names. Each has its own page with the same sections, namely sample design, versions, tables, linkage, and known issues.

  1. Sample Database

    • National Sample Cohort (표본코호트DB)
    • Health Screening Cohort (건강검진코호트DB)
    • Senior Cohort (노인코호트DB)
    • Low-Risk Sample Dataset (저위험 표본데이터셋)

  2. Customized Database

    • Customized Research DB (맞춤형연구DB)

The documents each page follows, and the conflicts found between them, are listed on the sources and versions page. The NHISS portal also lists an educational sample research DB (교육용 표본연구DB), which is not documented here.

A shared concept does not guarantee a shared coding. For example, SGG and SIDO differ in geographic detail, and the disability and premium variables were regrouped at different times in different databases.

docs.title: Page template
docs.text:
A new dataset page should use the following sections, leaving out a section when the information is not yet known.

  • Overview. What population the database covers and what it is typically used for.
  • Sample design. How the sample was drawn, including the base year, strata, and sampling fraction.
  • Versions. Each release, its years of coverage, and what changed between releases.
  • Tables. The tables in the database, with Korean and English names and their unit of observation.
  • Linkage. How tables link to one another, with the Korean and English names of each identifier.
  • Known issues. Pitfalls specific to this database.

docs.title: Customized Research DB (맞춤형연구DB)
docs.text:
A customized research DB (맞춤형연구DB) is extracted from the full National Health Information Database (국민건강정보DB) for one approved study. It can include everyone who meets the study criteria rather than a sample, within limits set by the NHIS, which makes it the route for rare conditions, small areas, and sensitive diagnoses that the cohort databases mask.

Sources

This page follows the customized DB application form (맞춤형 자료 요청서) of 2026, the column layouts of the customized DB dated September 10, 2026, the NHIS guide to new applications (사용자매뉴얼1, 연구용DB 신규신청 방법, version 4.0, September 2024), and the NHISS portal. Every table and variable is documented in the codebook.

docs.title: Building the extract
docs.text:
The applicant first defines the study population and then chooses the tables and variables to extract. The portal divides the application into six steps.

Step 한글 Content 1 연구신청 Research application 2 구축방식선택 Choice of how the extract is built 3 분석주제설정 Research topic 4 대상자조건설정 Conditions that define the study population 5 추출변수설정 Tables and variables to extract 6 최종확인 Final confirmation

The extract can be built in three ways (자료추출방식), and the choice determines who turns the request into code.

  • Standard extraction (기본추출). NHIS staff build the extract from an Excel request form that the applicant downloads, fills in, and uploads.
  • Automated extraction (자동화추출). The applicant sets the conditions and variables on the portal, and the extract is built exactly as set there.
  • Researcher extraction (연구자추출). The researcher visits NHIS headquarters and builds the extract in person, after uploading the same Excel form and marking the project title with [연구자추출].

Whichever way is chosen, the definition of the study population in the research summary (연구과제요약서) must match the one on the portal or in the request form, and the requested years and tables must also match.

docs.title: Defining the study population
docs.text:
The request form defines the population by inclusion conditions and up to two exclusion conditions, and each condition combines the items below.

Item 한글 Example in the form Years 연도 2009 Diagnosis codes 상병코드 C22, including its subcodes Diagnosis position 주상병 / 부상병 Primary only, primary and the first secondary, or primary and all secondary diagnoses Special co-payment codes 산정특례 특정기호구분 V193, V194 Type of care 의과 / 한방 / 치과 / 약국 Medical care only Setting 입원 / 외래 Inpatient only Fee codes 행위수가코드 Q7221, following the fee codes of the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service Drug ingredient codes 약제주성분코드 130801ASY

The form also allows a separate definition of cases and controls, with the example of a control group five times the size of the case group drawn from the general population. Lists of more than 50 codes go on a separate sheet, and the NHIS may revise a population that exceeds 10 million people or an extract that is too large.

The claims of the population can be extracted in two ways, and the form asks for exactly one of them.

  • Matching claims only. Only the claims that meet the conditions, such as the claims with a liver cancer code in 2010 to 2012.
  • All claims of the population. Every claim of the people selected, such as all claims from 2008 to 2014 of people treated for liver cancer in 2009.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
The 2026 form divides the tables into basic tables, which any project can request, and additional tables, which the review committee grants only when the application states why each is needed. Data can be requested for 2002 to 2024, and each delivered file is named by its table and year, as in BFC_2002.

Table 한글 Group First year Codebook Eligibility and premiums (BFC) 자격 및 보험료 Basic 2002 BFC Death (DTH) 사망 Basic 2002 DTH Claim statements (T20) 명세서 Basic 2002 T20 Treatment details (T30) 진료내역 Basic 2002 T30 Diagnoses (T40) 상병내역 Basic 2002 T40 Prescriptions (T60) 처방전교부상세 Basic, with a drug use plan 2002 T60 General health screening, eligible population, results, and questionnaire 일반1차검진 대상자, 결과, 문진 Basic 2002 G1E_OBJ, G1E_RST, GQ_RST Healthcare providers 요양기관 Additional 2002 INST Long-term care 장기요양 Additional 2008 Four tables Cancer screening 암 검진 Additional 2002, with cervical cancer from 2005 and lung cancer from 2019 Six cancers and the questionnaire Infant and child screening 영유아 검진 Additional 2007 Eligible population and rounds 0 to 7 Mother and newborn linkage 산모-신생아 자료 Additional Through 2024 Linkage

A request for the prescription table (T60) must include a drug use plan (약제활용계획서) and a list of the drugs needed, and drugs missing from the list are not provided.1 Additional tables are requested by naming them under other requested data (요청자료-기타) and explaining, in the research methods, why each table is needed and how it will be used.

docs.title: How the extract differs from the cohort databases
docs.text:
The customized DB uses its own names and contains several fields that the cohort databases coarsen or omit.

  • Identifiers. People are identified by INDI_DSCM_NO (개인식별아이디), and the claims tables are linked by CMN_KEY (공통키).
  • Diagnoses. The claim statement table carries five diagnosis positions, SICK_SYM1 to SICK_SYM5.
  • Residence and premiums. The eligibility table records the district of actual residence (RVSN_ADDR_CD, 실거주주소코드), the premium amount (CALC_CTRB_FD), a premium vigintile (CALC_CTRB_VTILE_FD), and the six-digit industry of the workplace (INDTP_CD).
  • Death. The death table gives the date of death (DTH_ASSMD_DT, 사망일자) but not its cause.

Cause of death requires a separate request for the cause-of-death database of the national statistics agency (통계청사망원인DB), entered under other requested data. The 2024 application guide states that only the National Sample Cohort and the Health Screening Cohort include cause of death, so the other databases do not. The same guide gives income level and education level as examples of variables the NHIS does not provide.

docs.title: Versions of the layouts
docs.text:
The NHIS publishes the column layouts of the customized DB as Excel files on the portal (고객지원, 자료실, 맞춤형 레이아웃). The layouts of September 10, 2026 replace those of 2024, which differ in the points below.

  • Claim statements. T20 gained the provider type code (YOYANG_CLSFC_CD, 요양기관종별코드), for 28 variables.
  • Providers. The provider table moved from the main layout file to its own file (요양기관 자료 제공 컬럼 레이아웃).

The layouts for general health screening, cancer screening and its questionnaire, and infant and child screening were consulted only in their 2026 versions.

The application form of 2026 lets applicants request data through 2024, while the 2024 application guide allowed requests through 2023.

docs.title: Analysis environment
docs.text:
Researchers analyze customized extracts at NHIS analysis centers (분석센터). The cohort manuals add that research on the diagnoses and procedures they mask can be carried out without masking in designated analysis rooms, using customized data.

  1. The guide asks applicants to request drugs at the coarsest level that serves the study, such as groups or the first four digits of the ingredient code. ↩

docs.title: Health Screening Cohort (건강검진코호트DB)
docs.text:
The National Health Screening Cohort (NHIS-HEALS, 건강검진코호트DB) follows about 515,000 people who received a general health screening in 2002 or 2003 at ages 40 to 79. It links their eligibility, claims, health screening, and provider records from 2002 to 2023, and its screening data are richer than those of the sample cohort, with separate tables for the life-transition and oral screenings. Because members were selected on attending a screening and the cohort is never refreshed, it describes a screened and aging population rather than the general population.

Source

This page follows the NHIS user manual for the database (건강검진코호트DB 사용자 매뉴얼), version 2.3, which describes data through 2023.

docs.title: Sample design
docs.text:
The cohort is a simple random sample of adults who attended a general health screening at the start of the 2000s, with the design below.

  • Population (모집단). About 5.15 million people aged 40 to 79 at the end of December 2002 who held health insurance and received a general health screening in 2002 or 2003, each counted once.
  • Sampling (표본추출). A 10 percent simple random sample.
  • Sample (표본). 514,866 people.
  • Exclusions (제외). Foreigners are excluded because they are likely to leave the cohort. Medical Aid beneficiaries are excluded at baseline because they were not eligible for the general screening in 2002, although members who later move to Medical Aid stay in the cohort.

The lower age bound of 40 follows the screening rules of the time. Below age 40, only heads of self-employed households and employee insured were eligible for screening, so a younger sample would not have represented its age group.

The cohort is closed, so it ages and shrinks over time. Membership falls from 514,866 in 2002 to 414,724 in 2023 through death and loss of eligibility, and every member is 61 or older by 2023.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The manual describes the current data through 2023 but does not record earlier releases. The files are split into the periods 2002 to 2015, 2016 to 2019, and 2020 to 2023, and several variables differ in the files from 2016 onward, as listed under known issues.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
The database has 46 files in seven groups of tables.

Table 한글 Files Unit of observation Years Variables Eligibility 자격 DB NHIS_HEALS_JK (3 files) Person and year 2002-2023 12 Claims 진료 DB NHIS_HEALS_GY20 to NHIS_HEALS_GY60 (30 files) Claim, line item, diagnosis, or prescribed drug 2002-2023 6 to 21 per table General health screening 일반건강검진 NHIS_HEALS_GJ (4 files) Screening 2002-2023 Varies by period Life-transition screening 생애전환기 건강진단 NHIS_HEALS_LJ (2 files) Screening 2007-2017 69 Oral screening 구강검진 NHIS_HEALS_GO (3 files) Screening 2002-2023 Varies by period Oral life-transition screening 구강검진 (생애) NHIS_HEALS_LO Screening 2007-2015 Varies by period Providers 요양기관 DB NHIS_HEALS_YK (3 files) Provider and year 2002-2023 10

Unlike the sample cohort, the eligibility table records AGE (연령, age) as age in completed years at the end of each year, and death as an exact date in DTH_MDY (사망일자, date of death).

docs.title: Claims tables
docs.text:
Claims are split by claim form into three groups, which differ from the four groups of the sample cohort. File names combine the table, the period, and the group, as in NHIS_HEALS_GY20_0215_T1.

Group 한글 Claim form codes, FORM_CD (서식코드, claim form) Tables T1, medical and public health 의과·보건기관 02 and 03 medical inpatient and outpatient, 07 and 08 public health inpatient and outpatient, 09 psychiatric day ward, 10 and 11 psychiatric inpatient and outpatient 20t, 30t, 40t, 60t T2, dental and Korean medicine 치과·한방 04 and 05 dental inpatient and outpatient, 12 and 13 Korean medicine inpatient and outpatient 20t, 30t, 40t, 60t T3, pharmacy 약국 20 dispensing without prescription (약국 조제), 21 dispensing by prescription (처방 조제) 20t, 30t Table 한글 Unit of observation Variables 20t, claims 명세서 Claim 20 (21 for pharmacy) 30t, treatment details 진료내역 Line item on a claim 14 (18 for dental and Korean medicine) 40t, diagnoses 상병내역 Diagnosis on a claim 6 60t, prescriptions 처방전교부상세내역 Drug on a prescription filled outside the provider 11

docs.title: Screening tables
docs.text: General screening covers 2002 to 2023, and from 2018 it absorbs the life-transition screening (생애전환기 건강진단) given at ages 40 and 66, which has its own table for 2007 to 2017. Oral screening has a general table and a life-transition table through 2015, and a combined table from 2014.

docs.title: Linkage
docs.text:
Only the eligibility, claims header, and screening tables carry the person identifier, so the claims detail tables reach a person through the claim identifier.

Variable 한글 English Links PERSON_ID 개인일련번호 Person identifier Eligibility, claims header (20t), and screening KEY_SEQ 청구일련번호 Claim identifier 20t, 30t, 40t, and 60t of the same claim group YKIHO_ID 요양기관식별대체번호 Provider identifier Claims header (20t) and providers MPRSC_ISSUE_ADMIN_ID 처방전발행기관식별대체번호 Prescribing provider identifier Pharmacy claims header (T3 20t) to the prescribing provider

Pharmacy claims can be linked to the claim of the provider that wrote the prescription. The manual matches PERSON_ID (개인일련번호, person identifier), MPRSC_ISSUE_ADMIN_ID (처방전발행기관식별대체번호, prescribing provider identifier) against YKIHO_ID (요양기관식별대체번호, provider identifier), and TOT_PRES_DD_CNT (총처방일수, total days prescribed). Drugs dispensed without a prescription have no prescribing provider to match.

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
The following features of the database commonly lead to errors.

  • Selection on screening. Members attended a screening in 2002 or 2003, so they differ from adults who do not attend, and estimates do not generalize to all adults aged 40 to 79 without adjustment.
  • Closed cohort. No members are added, so later years describe an older population only, and the youngest members are 61 by 2023.
  • Medical Aid claims before 2006. Claims filed under Medical Aid before January 1, 2006 are excluded, while claims for earlier care that were filed after that date are included.
  • Province only. Residence is recorded only as SIDO (시도코드, province), with 17 provinces, so district-level analysis is not possible.
  • Premium deciles are household measures. CTRB_PT_TYPE_CD (보험료분위, premium decile) runs from 0 for Medical Aid to 10, and every member of a household shares the decile of the household. A missing category appears only from 2016.
  • Variables change in the files from 2016. GNL_NM_CD (일반명코드, generic name code) is dropped and DIV_CD (분류코드, item code) takes its place. The severe category of DFAB_GRD_CD (장애중증도코드, disability severity) widens from grades 1 and 2 to grades 1 to 3, and notifiable infectious diseases (법정감염병) become masked.
  • Sensitive diagnoses are masked, with exceptions. Diagnosis codes on the list of 3,116 sensitive codes show only their first letter and an underscore. Codes needed to interpret screening results stay unmasked, namely acute hepatitis (B16, B17), dementia (F00-F03), and depressive and mood disorders (F32-F34, F38, F39).
  • Screening layouts change in 2009 and 2018. The 2009 and 2018 reforms changed the tests, the questionnaire, and the variable names, so multi-year analyses need to check that each variable measures the same thing over time.
  • Screenings are not annual. Members can skip a screening in an eligible year or attend in another year, so the screening tables do not form a balanced annual panel.
  • Implausible screening values are already missing. Test results outside the manual's plausibility ranges were set to missing before release.
  • Medical Aid screenings before 2012. The NHIS screened Medical Aid beneficiaries only from 2012, but people listed for screening before they moved to Medical Aid can still appear in earlier years.
  • Missing causes of death. Some deaths have no cause because the death record did not link to the national cause-of-death data, for example after a correction to the resident registration number.
  • Providers appear only in years with claims. The provider table includes a provider only in years when a cohort member used it.
  • Bundled and per diem payment hides detail. Claims paid by diagnosis-related group (포괄수가제) or at per diem rates, as in long-term care hospitals, report little detail on individual services and drugs.
  • Variable names differ from the sample cohort. The database uses an older naming convention, so code written for the sample cohort does not run without renaming. The crosswalk maps the main variables.

docs.title: Low-Risk Sample Dataset (저위험 표본데이터셋)
docs.text:
The Low-Risk Sample Dataset (저위험 표본데이터셋) is a heavily aggregated sample built to widen access to NHIS data for private-sector research and development. It follows 1,000,000 randomly sampled people who used medical care between 2014 and 2023, with one record per person, year, and main diagnosis group, together with their health screening results. The NHISS portal lists it as the low-risk sample cohort (저위험 표본코호트DB) in its menu for applying for sample research databases (표본연구DB신청). The portal's pages describing each database do not yet include it, and it is absent from the NHIS guide to new applications of September 2024.

Source

This page follows the NHIS user manual for the dataset (저위험 표본데이터셋 사용자 매뉴얼), which is undated and covers data through 2023.

docs.title: Sample design
docs.text:
The sample is drawn from people who used medical care in the ten-year window, with the design below.

  • Population (모집단). Everyone with at least one medical claim (의과 요양급여청구명세서) between 2014 and 2023, each counted once.
  • Sample (표본). 1,000,000 people drawn at random, with RN_INDI (개인일련번호, person identifier) assigned at random from 1 to 1,000,000.
  • Years (기간). Care from 2014 to 2023 and deaths from 2014 to 2024.

Because the sample is drawn from people who used care, people with no medical claims in the ten years are absent, which matters for any estimate of prevalence or utilization rates in the population. The manual reports that the sample resembles the population in its sex ratio, regional distribution, and mean age.

docs.text:
The dataset has two tables, plus two lookup files for diagnosis names (SMPL_MC_SICK_NM) and the list of masked diagnoses (SMPL_MC_SICK_MSK).

The screening table holds 23 measurements and questionnaire items, including height, weight, waist circumference, blood pressure, blood and urine tests, estimated kidney function, smoking, drinking, and physical activity.

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
The dataset trades detail for ease of access, and the following features limit what it can answer.

  • Diagnoses are coarse. Only the main diagnosis is recorded, at the level of a KCD block (중분류) or, for sensitive diagnoses, a KCD chapter (대분류). Eight major cancers are kept at a finer level, namely stomach (C16), colorectal (C18-C20), liver (C22), gallbladder and biliary (C23-C24), pancreas (C25), lung (C33-C34), kidney (C64), and thyroid (C73), while breast and cervical cancer appear only at the chapter level because they are sensitive.
  • Only medical claims are included. Dental, Korean medicine, and pharmacy claims are excluded, and the data contain no costs, dates of care, procedures, drugs, or providers.
  • Days are annual totals. Inpatient and outpatient days are summed by year and diagnosis group and capped at the number of days in the year, so individual visits and admissions cannot be identified.
  • Screening values are rounded and top-coded. Height, weight, and waist circumference are top-coded at 190 cm, 126 kg, and 121 cm, and several measurements are rounded to whole numbers.
  • Questionnaire items are harmonized. Responses were recoded to be comparable across screening reforms, with drinking frequency per month converted to a weekly rate. Walking days exist only through 2017, and muscle-strengthening days only from 2018.
  • Birth year is top-coded. BTH_YYYY (출생연도, birth year) is recorded as 1929LE for people aged 85 or older in 2014.
  • Triglyceride entry in the manual. The manual's description of G1E_TG (트리글리세라이드, triglycerides) gives the formula for calculated LDL cholesterol, which appears to belong to G1E_LDL (LDL-콜레스테롤, LDL cholesterol).

  1. The manual's text gives 45,814,155 medical use records, but its table gives 42,814,155, and only the second figure is consistent with its reported total of 45,587,172 records across both tables. ↩

docs.title: National Sample Cohort (표본코호트DB)
docs.text:
The National Sample Cohort (NHIS-NSC, 표본코호트DB) follows a 2 percent sample of the Korean population from 2002 to 2023. It links eligibility, premium, claims, health screening, death, provider, and long-term care records for about one million people drawn from the 2006 population. The sample covers all ages and includes Medical Aid beneficiaries, which makes it the standard NHIS database for population-level research, and the NHIS reports that it supports more than 300 projects every year.

Source

This page follows the NHIS user manual for the database (표본코호트DB 사용자 매뉴얼), version 1.5 of May 2026, which describes release 2.2 with data through 2023.

docs.title: Sample design
docs.text:
The current release samples people enrolled throughout 2006, a change from the 2002 population used by the first release. The NHIS moved the base year because it began processing Medical Aid claims in 2006, so a 2006 sample has complete claims for every member from that year forward.

The main sample is a stratified draw from the 2006 population, with the design below.

  • Population (모집단). Korean nationals with health insurance or Medical Aid eligibility for all of 2006, a total of 48,222,537 people.
  • Strata (층화). The 2,142 strata cross sex, 17 age groups, 3 area types, and 21 insurance and premium groups. Age groups are five-year bands from age 1 to 79 plus a group for 80 and older. Area types are large cities (대도시), small and medium cities (중소도시), and rural areas (농어촌), and the insurance and premium groups are Medical Aid plus ten premium deciles each for self-employed and employee insured.
  • Sample (표본). 1,000,000 people, or 2.1 percent of the population.

docs.title: Supplementary samples
docs.text:
Two kinds of supplementary samples are added to the main sample, and every member's sample type is recorded in SMPL_TYPE_CD (표본구분, sample type). The person identifier RN_INDI (개인고유번호, person identifier) encodes the same information through its range.

Sample 한글 SMPL_TYPE_CD RN_INDI range Members in 2006 Members in 2023 Main sample 2006년 전국민 표본 1 1 to 1,000,000 1,000,000 902,203 Missing-premium supplement 2006년 정상적 보험료 결측군 추가표본 2 1,000,001 to 2,000,000 11,638 10,635 Newborn supplement 신생아 추가 표본 3 2,000,001 to 3,000,000 9,355 157,531 Newborn missing-premium supplement 신생아 정상적 보험료 결측군 추가표본 4 3,000,001 to 4,000,000 215 5,212 Total 합계 1,021,208 1,075,581

The missing-premium supplement covers people whose premium is legitimately missing in the administrative records. Examples include career soldiers and members of the longshore workers' union, whose premiums are not levied on individuals, and workers on long-term leave, whose premiums are billed afterward.

The newborn supplements add a sample of each birth cohort from 2006 onward, drawn with the same design as the main sample.1 Without them, the main sample is a closed cohort that ages every year and shrinks from 1,000,000 members in 2006 to 902,203 in 2023. Studies that need a representative cross-section of a later year therefore need the newborn supplements, while studies that follow the 2006 population need the main and missing-premium samples.

docs.title: Retrospective years
docs.text:
The years 2002 to 2005 are observed retrospectively for people enrolled throughout 2006, and they differ from later years in three ways.

  • No deaths. Every member survived to 2006, so the data contain no deaths from 2002 to 2005. The main sample also has no deaths in 2006, and the 7 deaths recorded that year are all newborns.
  • Survivor selection. People who died or emigrated before 2006 are absent, so the 2002 to 2005 data are not a sample of the population alive in those years.
  • No Medical Aid claims. Claims of Medical Aid beneficiaries are missing for 2002 to 2005, because the NHIS began processing them only in 2006.

docs.text:

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
The following features of the database commonly lead to errors, beyond the retrospective years described above.

  • Sensitive diagnoses are masked. Diagnosis codes in T20 and T40 that belong to a list of 3,116 sensitive codes show only their first letter and an underscore, so A15 appears as A_. The list combines special diagnoses (공단 특수상병) and notifiable infectious diseases (법정감염병), including all mental and behavioral disorders (F00-F99), pregnancy and childbirth (O00-O99), congenital anomalies (Q00-Q99), and cancers of the breast and genital organs (C50-C63). Research on these conditions requires a customized research DB.
  • Sensitive procedures are masked. Fee codes in T30 for genitourinary, breast, and obstetric procedures, including cesarean sections and abortions, are masked in the same way.
  • Excluded diagnoses are dropped. T40 omits diagnoses that the provider marked as excluded once the final diagnosis was confirmed (배제상병), so SICK_CLSF_TYPE (상병분류구분코드, diagnosis type) takes only the values 1 for primary and 2 for secondary. The variable is populated only from 2004.
  • Claim counts change around 2011. Outpatient billing moved from one claim per month to one claim per visit day, a change extended to hospitals in 2011, so the number of claims changes even where the number of visits does not.
  • Premium deciles shift after the 2018 and 2022 reforms. Premium reforms in July 2018 and September 2022 expanded the group paying the minimum premium, which bunches self-employed insured into the lowest decile. In the manual's tables, the first self-employed decile grows from 15,757 members in 2018 to 58,379 in 2019, and by 2023 the second to fourth self-employed deciles are empty.
  • Premium deciles are relative to insurance type and household. CTRB_Q10 (보험료 10분위, premium decile) is computed separately for employee and self-employed insured, and every person on the same insurance card shares the decile of the household.
  • Premiums lag income. CTRB_Q10 for 2023 reflects 2022 income and property, while INC_FML_EQ100 (균등화가구소득 100분위, equivalized household income percentile) for 2023 reflects 2023 income. The premium decile is also measured at the start of the year, and the household percentiles at the end.
  • Property percentiles are mostly missing before 2006. Values of PRP_FML_EQ100 (균등화가구재산 100분위, equivalized household property percentile) are largely missing for reference years 2005 and earlier, because the 2006 tax reform redefined property tax items.
  • District codes are harmonized within years and partly merged. SGG (시군구, district) is converted to the code valid on January 1 of each year, and invalid codes are replaced with the nearest valid code, so codes still differ across years when boundaries change. Four small counties are merged into neighbors, namely Ongjin into Ganghwa, Yanggu into Hwacheon, Yeongyang into Cheongsong, and Ulleung into Uljin.
  • Birth year is top-coded. BTH_YYYY (출생연도, birth year) is recorded as 1921LE for people born in 1921 or earlier, so the variable is stored as text and age is censored at 85 in 2006.
  • Disability severity was regrouped. DSB_SVRT_CD (장애중증도구분, disability severity) counts grades 1 to 3 as severe from release 2.1, compared with grades 1 and 2 in release 2.0.
  • Life-transition screenings are not included. The screening table holds general health screenings only. People aged 40 and 66 were screened under the separate life-transition program (생애전환기 건강진단) from 2007 to 2017, so their screenings at those ages are missing for those years.
  • Screening content changes in 2009 and 2018. The screening table has 51 variables for 2002 to 2008, 57 for 2009 to 2017, and 113 for 2018 to 2023, and questionnaire items and response categories changed with each reform. Fasting glucose replaced pre-meal glucose in 2010, and Medical Aid beneficiaries appear in the screening data only from 2012.
  • Drugs are identified by ingredient, not product. Product codes were removed in release 2.0, so drugs are identified by GNL_NM_CD (일반명코드, generic name code) and EFMDC_CLSF_NO (약효분류번호, efficacy classification number).
  • Per diem payment hides detail. Long-term care hospitals (요양병원) and public health centers paid at per diem rates report little detail on individual services and drugs.
  • Rare conditions have few cases. Because the sample has about one million members, the NHIS advises applicants to check case counts before proposing a study of a rare condition.

  1. The manual's text says newborn sampling began in 2007, but its tables include 9,597 newborns born in 2006. Its count of newborns by birth year also sums to 147,548, fewer than the 162,743 newborn-supplement members it reports for 2023, and the manual does not explain either difference. ↩

  2. Years for release 1.0 are from Lee et al. (2017). The current manual does not document release 1.0. ↩

docs.title: Senior Cohort (노인코호트DB)
docs.text:
The Senior Cohort (NHIS-Senior, 노인코호트DB) follows an 8 percent sample of people aged 60 to 80 in 2008 and adds a sample of new 60-year-olds every year. It links eligibility, claims, health screening, provider, and long-term care insurance records, with claims from 2002 to 2023 and long-term care records from 2008 to 2023. The NHIS built it for research on the risk factors and prognosis of diseases of old age, and it offers a much larger sample of older people than the sample cohort.

Source

This page follows the NHIS user manual for the database (노인코호트DB 사용자 매뉴얼), version 1.4, which describes release 2.0 with data through 2023.

docs.title: Sample design
docs.text:
The current release samples older adults enrolled in 2008 and refreshes the sample with each new cohort of 60-year-olds, with the design below.

  • Population (모집단). People aged 60 to 80 in January 2008 who held health insurance or Medical Aid eligibility throughout that year, a total of 6,399,533 people.
  • Sampling (표본추출). An 8 percent sample stratified by sex, single year of age, area type, and premium decile.1
  • Sample (표본). 511,953 people.
  • Refreshment (신규대상자). From 2009, an 8 percent sample of the people turning 60 is added every year, between 34,423 and 72,977 people a year.
  • Exclusions (제외). Foreigners are excluded because they are likely to leave the cohort.

Each member's origin is recorded in SMPL_GRP_TYPE (표본형태 구분, sample type), which is 1 for the 2008 sample and 2 for members added from 2009.

docs.title: Records before entry
docs.text:
Refreshment members enter the data ten years before the year they were sampled, so the eligibility table contains people in their fifties. The table grows from 664,193 people in 2002 to 1,124,873 in 2023, and only 332,385 of the people in 2023 belong to the 2008 sample. Analyses of older adults therefore need to restrict each year to the relevant ages, rather than use every record in the eligibility table.

The 2008 sample is observed retrospectively from 2002 to 2007 and had to remain enrolled through 2008. Its first deaths therefore appear in 2009, and its records before 2008 exclude people who died before 2008.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
Release 2.0 is a new sample of a different population, not an extension of release 1.0.

Release 1.0 Release 2.0 Provided December 2015 to September 2021 September 2021 to present Population Aged 60 and older in December 2002, about 5.5 million Aged 60 to 80 in January 2008, about 6.4 million Sample 558,147, or 10 percent 511,953, or 8 percent, plus 8 percent of each new cohort of 60-year-olds Sampling Simple random Stratified by sex, age, area type, and premium decile Years 2002-2015, retrospective 2002-2023, retrospective and prospective Masked diagnoses 114 codes 3,116 codes Long-term care Includes the doctor's opinion form (의사소견서) Doctor's opinion form discontinued Severe disability Grades 1 and 2 Grades 1 to 3

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
The following features of the database commonly lead to errors, beyond the records before entry described above.

  • Cause of death may not be available. The manual lists DTH_CODE1 and DTH_CODE2 (사망원인1, 사망원인2, cause of death) and describes them as linked from the national statistics agency, but two other NHIS sources say the opposite. The NHISS portal's description of this database states that cause of death is not included. The NHIS guide to new applications (version 4.0, September 2024) likewise states that only the National Sample Cohort and the Health Screening Cohort include it. Applicants who need cause of death should confirm with the NHIS before applying.
  • Medical Aid claims before 2006. Claims filed under Medical Aid before January 1, 2006 are excluded, while claims for earlier care that were filed after that date are included.
  • Long-term care begins in July 2008. Long-term care insurance started in July 2008, so the 2008 records cover half a year.
  • Care grades changed in 2014. The grade system expanded from three grades to five in July 2014, and a cognitive support grade (인지지원등급) was added later. GJU_RCGT_GRADE_CD (등급판정인정등급코드, assessed care grade) is therefore not comparable across these changes.
  • Long-term care claims can be split. A facility can bill one person's care on several claims, so total days and costs of care must be summed by person.
  • Some long-term care claims have no facility. Claims for visiting-nurse orders under short-term care do not match any facility in T05.
  • Long-term care facilities are not providers. Long-term care facilities are separate institutions from the medical providers in the provider table, and they are described only in T05.
  • Province only. Residence is recorded only as SIDO (시도코드, province), with 17 provinces.
  • The income decile is a premium decile. The manual calls CTRB_PT_TYPE_CD an income decile (소득분위), but it is the same premium decile used in the other cohorts, computed for households and running from 0 for Medical Aid to 10.
  • Sensitive diagnoses are masked. Diagnosis codes on the list of 3,116 sensitive codes show only their first letter and an underscore.
  • Claims are cut off at a submission date. Claims for care in 2023 include those submitted through April 2025, so any later submissions are missing.
  • Bundled and per diem payment hides detail. Claims paid by diagnosis-related group (포괄수가제) or at per diem rates, as in long-term care hospitals, report little detail on individual services and drugs.
  • Variable names differ from the sample cohort. The database uses the same naming convention as the Health Screening Cohort. The crosswalk maps the main variables.

  1. The manual is inconsistent on this point. Its comparison of releases and the NHISS portal describe stratified sampling, while its sample design section describes simple random sampling. ↩

  2. The manual's table of join keys names this key LTC_MGNNU_SEQ_NO (장기요양신청_일련번호), while its code examples and notes use PERSON_SEQ. ↩

docs.title: Sources and versions
docs.text: Every dataset page and codebook entry on this site rests on an NHIS document, and this page records which version of each is followed. When the NHIS publishes a newer document, the older one is kept here as superseded so that readers can tell which description applies to their extract.

docs.title: Documents followed
docs.text:
The documents below were collected from the NHISS portal in October 2026. Dates are those printed in the documents or their file names, and a document with no printed date is marked as undated.
